newsitem.title: USA: CBOT considering Dow Jones stock index complex.
newsitem.headline: CBOT considering Dow Jones stock index complex.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade is considering listing derivatives on Dow Jones stock indexes, including the Dow Industrials, CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said Thursday.
"We have been involved for some time in discussions with Dow Jones & Co regarding developing the Dow product complex at the Chicago Board of Trade," Arbor said at CBOT's annual meeting.
"If and when Dow Jones decides to license their Industrial Average, we, the Board of Trade, will make a formal proposal," he added.
"Our proposal will seek to trade not only futures on the Industrial Average but on a full complex of Dow index products which include products of foreign countries," he said.

"While Dow Jones is near completing the steps necessary to make its decision, we have been advised that the process is very time-intensive and that they may not move as quickly as we might desire," he said.
The CBOT tried in the early 1980s to launch futures based on the Dow Industrials, but the publishing firm sued the exchange to stop the plan. The CBOT eventually lost the suit.

Earlier this week, Dow Jones & Co Inc said it was studying the possibility of licensing the Industrial average, arguably the most closely followed stock index in the world, but added that it had not yet decided to do so.
"We had a policy a number of years ago very much against it," Dow Jones spokesman Roger May told Reuters. "There was an effort to do it 15 years ago or so and we said 'no' -- but times changed."
Arbor said trading in the Dow indexes would be done in open-outcry pit during the day and on the Project A electronic system for after-hours business.
Arbor said he did not expect the CBOT to trade futures on individual stocks -- currently prohibited by law -- even if such a product was deregulated as proposed in a bill pending in Congress.
"Realistically, we don't have high hopes to be able to trade stock futures...because of jurisdictional problems between the securities industry and the banking industry," he said.
